package.name: cloudinary
package.packageFile:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/package.schema.json

# CLOUDINARY, fully declarative.
#
# It sat on the backlog as "blocked on `encoding: form`", and that turned out to be wrong twice over. The
# nodes used the Cloudinary SDK, so the blocker was inferred from the SDK's behaviour rather than from the
# HTTP API — and the HTTP API is kinder than the SDK:
#
#   SIGNING IS OPTIONAL. The SDK signs every upload (sorted params + api_secret, SHA-1), which the
#   expression sandbox cannot do — it has sha256 and no sha1. Cloudinary's docs offer HTTP Basic Auth
#   instead, explicitly "no signature calculation required", for the Upload API as well as the Admin API.
#   So `scheme: basic`, which already existed.
#
#   THE UPLOAD BODY IS A FORM, and their own curl example uses -F, which is multipart — the capability
#   built for ElevenLabs speech-to-text a moment earlier. `encoding: form` was never needed.
#
# The lesson is the one already recorded in the backlog: judge by the WIRE FORMAT, never by the client
# library a node happened to use.

name: cloudinary
displayName: Cloudinary
description: Upload, list and read media in Cloudinary
version: 2.0.0
category: media
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1754502687/gravity/icons/cloudinary_logo.png

features:
  - Upload images and video from a URL or base64
  - List and read media already in the account

allowedHosts:
  - api.cloudinary.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [basic]
  transport: [json]
  encoding: [multipart]

credentials.cloudinaryCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

# FIELD NAMES ARE SNAKE_CASE, unchanged, because that is what the stored credentials use — a credential is
# read by field name, so tidying these to camelCase would leave every existing workflow authenticating
# with three undefineds.
name: cloudinaryCredential
displayName: Cloudinary
description: Cloudinary API credentials for media management

properties:
  - name: cloud_name
    displayName: Cloud Name
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Your Cloudinary cloud name
  - name: api_key
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    # Was false, so this was stored in PLAINTEXT (SECURITY.md, 2026-08-30). Cloudinary signs
    # requests with api_key + api_secret together, so the pair IS the credential; treating
    # half of it as public is a distinction the database cannot act on. Only cloud_name is
    # genuinely public here, because it appears in every delivery URL.
    secret: true
    description: Your Cloudinary API key
  - name: api_secret
    displayName: API Secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Cloudinary API secret

shared.credential.yaml:
# BASIC AUTH, and it is the reason this package needed no new capability.
#
# The SDK these nodes used signs every upload: sorted params, appended api_secret, SHA-1 — and the sandbox
# has no sha1, so that path would have needed a signing scheme in the executor. Cloudinary's own docs
# offer a way out: "Authenticate using your API Key and API Secret via HTTP Basic Auth (no signature
# calculation required)". Both the Admin API and the Upload API accept it.
#
# So all three nodes authenticate the same way, and the executor already had `basic`.

scheme: basic
username: "{{ credentials.cloudinaryCredential.api_key }}"
password: "{{ credentials.cloudinaryCredential.api_secret }}"

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: url
  value: "return response.url || ''"

- emit: secureUrl
  value: "return response.secure_url || response.url || ''"

- emit: publicId
  value: "return response.public_id || ''"

- emit: format
  value: "return response.format || ''"

- emit: metadata
  value: >-
    return {
      width: response.width,
      height: response.height,
      bytes: response.bytes,
      createdAt: response.created_at,
      tags: response.tags || []
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE POST to the Upload API, as a FORM — which is what Cloudinary's own curl example sends (`-F`).
#
# NO SIGNATURE, and that is the whole reason this node needed no new capability. The SDK it replaces signs
# every upload (sorted params + api_secret, SHA-1) and the expression sandbox has no sha1. Cloudinary's
# docs offer Basic Auth instead — "no signature calculation required" — for the Upload API as well as the
# Admin API, so `scheme: basic` does the job and the signing never has to be described.
#
# THE RESOURCE TYPE IS IN THE PATH, so the url is an expression: it defaults rather than producing
# `/v1_1/cloud//upload`, a URL that 404s about a route instead of about a missing field.

- name: upload
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return 'https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/'
      + credentials.cloudinaryCredential.cloud_name
      + '/' + (config.resourceType || 'image') + '/upload'
  credential: { $ref: credential }
  encoding: multipart

  body:
    # BARE BASE64 GETS A DATA URI, transcribed from the service: Cloudinary needs to be told what the
    # bytes are, and a naked base64 string is rejected. A URL or an existing data: URI passes through.
    file: >-
      return (() => {
        const d = String(config.imageData || '');
        return (d.startsWith('data:') || d.startsWith('http')) ? d : 'data:image/png;base64,' + d;
      })();
    folder: "{{ config.folder }}"
    # THE SANITISER IS TRANSCRIBED, step for step, because Cloudinary rejects an id with an extension or
    # punctuation and the code version quietly fixed both rather than failing: drop the extension, replace
    # anything outside [A-Za-z0-9_-/] with an underscore, collapse runs, trim the ends.
    public_id: >-
      return String(config.publicId || '').trim()
        ? String(config.publicId)
            .replace(/\.[^/.]+$/, '')
            .replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_\-\/]/g, '_')
            .replace(/_+/g, '_')
            .replace(/^_|_$/g, '')
        : undefined
    # A COMMA LIST BECOMES A TRIMMED ONE. Cloudinary accepts a comma-separated string, so this normalises
    # spacing rather than converting to an array — the form field is text either way.
    tags: >-
      return String(config.tags || '').trim()
        ? String(config.tags).split(',').map(t => t.trim()).filter(t => t).join(',')
        : undefined
    # Sent as the STRING "true"/"false" because a form carries text, and the default matches the service.
    overwrite: "return config.overwrite ? 'true' : 'false'"

  timeoutMs: 300000
  transport: json

  # Cloudinary answers 4xx with { error: { message } }, which names the real reason — an invalid public id,
  # an unsupported format, a quota. Surfaced as-is rather than replaced by a guess.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error.message || 'Cloudinary upload failed'"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [imageData, folder]
  properties:
    imageData:
      type: string
      title: File
      description: >-
        A URL Cloudinary can fetch, a data URI, or bare base64. Bare base64 is given a
        data:image/png;base64, prefix automatically, matching the code version.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    folder:
      type: string
      title: Folder
      # REQUIRED, deliberately. Cloudinary will happily accept no folder and drop the asset in the account
      # ROOT, which is unmanageable the moment a workflow uploads more than a handful — nothing groups,
      # nothing is findable, and nothing can be deleted in bulk later. The code version allowed it; this
      # does not, which is the one place this node is deliberately stricter than what it replaces.
      description: Folder to store the asset in. Every upload belongs in one.
      default: generated
    publicId:
      type: string
      title: Public ID
      description: >-
        Name for the asset. Any file extension is stripped and characters Cloudinary rejects become
        underscores, so a filename can be passed straight in. Leave blank for a generated id.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    tags:
      type: string
      title: Tags
      description: Comma-separated tags, e.g. "cover,generated"
      default: ""
    resourceType:
      type: string
      title: Resource Type
      description: What kind of asset this is. Cloudinary treats each differently.
      enum: [image, video, raw, auto]
      enumNames: [Image, Video, Raw, Auto-detect]
      default: image
    overwrite:
      type: boolean
      title: Overwrite
      description: Replace an existing asset with the same public id
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
"ui:order": [imageData, folder, publicId, tags, resourceType, overwrite]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Upstream data. The file itself is named in config, usually templated from here.
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: url
    type: string
    description: The asset's http URL
  - name: secureUrl
    type: string
    description: The asset's https URL — prefer this one
  - name: publicId
    type: string
    description: Cloudinary's id for the asset, for later transformation or deletion
  - name: format
    type: string
    description: The stored format, e.g. png
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: width, height, bytes, createdAt, tags

credentials:
  - name: cloudinaryCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/node.schema.json

type: CloudinaryUpload
kind: PromiseNode

name: Cloudinary Upload
category: Media & Design
color: "#3448C5"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1754502687/gravity/icons/cloudinary_logo.png

description: Upload an image or video to Cloudinary and get back a hosted URL.

whenToUse: >-
  Put a generated or fetched file into Cloudinary and get a durable hosted URL back. Reach for it whenever
  something downstream needs a LINK rather than bytes: base64 does not survive a chat message, an email or
  a browser page well, and a Cloudinary URL does.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: uploading twice creates two assets, and a reused answer would point at the older one.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/test.schema.json

# Running it live needs CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME, CLOUDINARY_API_KEY and CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET, and it WRITES
# to your account — the folder below keeps the test assets together so they are easy to find and delete.
#
# The source is Cloudinary's own demo image, so the fixture does not depend on a file of yours existing.

testData:
  config:
    imageData: https://res.cloudinary.com/demo/image/upload/sample.jpg
    folder: unoverse-test
    resourceType: image
    overwrite: true
  inputs:
    signal:
      url: https://res.cloudinary.com/demo/image/upload/sample.jpg
  expect:
    # HTTPS specifically. `secureUrl` falls back to `url` if the vendor omits it, and that fallback is
    # exactly what would hide an http-only response.
    secureUrl: "return output.secureUrl.startsWith('https://')"
    publicId: "return output.publicId.startsWith('unoverse-test/')"
    metadata: "return output.metadata.bytes > 0 && output.metadata.width > 0"
